I'm using a pair of Asus 980 Ti STRIX factory overclocked cards.

They run very hot, but the only thing faster than these would be Titans.

Most games run okay, but sometimes I need to cut the anti aliasing.

This would depend on your monitor... if you're on a laptop, yeah, you don't. But I'm using a very tidy Benq 32" BL3201PT. I've come from a 32" 1080p monitor, so the culture shock is a bit lower, but you still get the feeling you're pushing the envelope. Maybe several envelopes. You can still see pixels even on the brilliant BL3201PT (if you're on the fence about this monitor, and I know some readers will be, then you need be shoved over, it's brilliant, you need it, sell your car and buy one).

I've run this system for a while... it's extremely expensive, probably more like looking at how PC gaming will be in 2-3 years time, but today (I've overclocked my Skylake to a solid 4.6GHz to keep up with the monstrous STRIX cards). This system is not everyday... water cooled, the CPU is perfect, Intel have once again upped the bar. But the GPUs are infernos... the heat pushing out of the case is intense. However, in terms of visuals, the gaming experience is magnified considerably. New games shine as they were meant to do... but old games gain a sharpness and precision that they lacked. And it's surprising how many games will tolerate the higher resolution!

I solidly recommend the move to 4K, if you have the money to do so today. If you don't, and there is no shame in this, you're still a PC gamer and rightfully the best gaming experience will be yours, wait for the good things to come. Pascal may or may not bring the experience closer... but it is inevitable.

Regardless, at 32", you will see some pixellation and jaggies (neat, tiny little ones, but jaggies nonetheless) if you don't run antialiasing. FSAA is always better , if you have the horsepower to keep your framerates tolerable.

Im using a 27" Screen, so granted the visibility is not as good as a 32" screens, and i did not say that you cannot see the lack of antialiasing.
